title: Himalayan Divisions, Passes and Glaciers

cards.h: A favourite for map and fact questions
cards.b: The Himalaya appear in prelims through peaks, passes, glaciers and ranges, and in mains through hazards, rivers and strategy. This lesson goes beyond the basic three ranges to give the regional pattern, the key passes and the glaciers you must recall.

North of the Great Himalaya lies the Trans-Himalaya: the Karakoram, Ladakh and Zaskar ranges. The Karakoram holds K2 (8,611 m), the world's second highest peak, now in Pakistan-administered territory. Kanchenjunga (8,586 m) on the Sikkim-Nepal border is the highest peak in India. Nanda Devi (7,816 m) is the highest peak lying wholly within India.

Sidney Burrard divided the Himalaya by rivers: Punjab Himalaya (Indus to Satluj), Kumaon Himalaya (Satluj to Kali), Nepal Himalaya (Kali to Tista) and Assam Himalaya (Tista to Dihang). Beyond the Dihang, the Purvanchal hills (Patkai, Naga, Manipur, Mizo) turn south.

Pir Panjal is the longest range of the Lesser Himalaya. Others: Dhauladhar, Nag Tibba, Mussoorie and Mahabharat. The Kashmir valley lies between the Pir Panjal and the Great Himalaya. Other valleys: Kangra and Kullu. Hill stations include Shimla, Mussoorie, Nainital and Darjeeling. Between the Lesser Himalaya and the Shiwalik are the duns, such as Dehradun.

• Banihal (Pir Panjal): Jammu to Srinagar, with the Jawahar tunnel.
  • Zoji La: Srinagar to Leh, on the Great Himalaya.
  • Khardung La: Leh to Nubra valley, among the world's highest motorable roads.
  • Nathu La and Jelep La: Sikkim to Tibet.
  • Shipki La: Himachal Pradesh to Tibet; the Satluj enters India here.
  • Lipulekh and Niti: Uttarakhand to Tibet.
  • Bomdi La and Dihang in Arunachal Pradesh. Rohtang in Himachal; the Atal Tunnel (2020) passes below it.

The Himalaya hold the largest ice outside the poles, called the 'Third Pole'. Siachen (about 70 km, Karakoram, Nubra river source). Gangotri (about 30 km, source of the Bhagirathi, whose snout is at Gaumukh). Zemu (Sikkim, Kanchenjunga). Pindari, Milam (Kumaon). Baltoro and Biafo are in Pakistan-administered Karakoram. Kolahoi is in Kashmir.

The snow line is the height above which snow stays all year. It lies near 4,500-6,000 m in the Himalaya, lower on the wet eastern side. Himalayan glaciers are mostly valley glaciers. A cirque glacier sits in an armchair hollow. A piedmont glacier spreads at the foot of a mountain. India's cold desert in Ladakh sits in the rain shadow of the Great Himalaya.

ICIMOD's 2023 Hindu Kush Himalaya report found that glaciers are melting faster than in earlier decades. A glacial lake outburst flood (GLOF) hit Kedarnath in 2013 and South Lhonak lake in Sikkim in October 2023. The Chamoli disaster of February 2021 was a rock-ice avalanche. Scientists still debate how much loss is due to warming and how much to black carbon.

Passes shape border trade and defence: Nathu La reopened for trade with China in 2006. Roads and tunnels such as the Atal Tunnel and Zojila tunnel project improve all-weather access. The Himalaya are also a water tower for the Indus, Ganga and Brahmaputra, so glacier change is a food and energy security issue.

Likely questions: 'Himalayan glaciers and climate change', 'Strategic significance of passes', 'Regional divisions of the Himalaya'.

  • Match each pass to a state and a neighbour country.
  • Use a labelled outline map: Pir Panjal, Zaskar, Karakoram, Purvanchal.
  • For glaciers: causes, risks (GLOFs, flood, drought) and responses (early warning, hydropower rules).

quiz.q: The highest peak in India is?
quiz.w: Kanchenjunga, 8,586 m, is the highest in India.
It is the highest peak wholly in India.

quiz.q: The longest range of the Lesser Himalaya is?
Shipki La is on which river's entry route?

quiz.w: It is the Nubra valley's source.
Punjab, Kumaon, Nepal, Assam Himalaya are separated by rivers.

quiz.q: Which hill range lies east of the Dihang gorge?
quiz.w: Purvanchal hills turn south into northeast India.
